source.text:
Shopping for a smartphone under ₹20,000 in India has never offered more choice, or more confusion. Almost every phone in the bracket is 5G, most have 120Hz or faster screens, and a 50MP main camera is now the baseline. But if your priorities are a battery that genuinely lasts, software support that keeps the phone safe for years, and decent photos of children in a dim living room, the shortlist gets much shorter. We compared the most popular models on exactly those three points, and the answer is not the one most buyers expect.

Start with battery, because this is where the segment has moved fastest. Samsung still builds the Galaxy A17 5G and Galaxy M17 5G around 5,000mAh cells, which comfortably cover a full day. The Redmi 15 5G, Oppo K13 5G and Realme P4x 5G, however, all pack 7,000mAh batteries, and the Vivo T4x 5G sits at 6,500mAh. In practice a 7,000mAh phone is a two-day device for most people, which matters when you are recording a school function or a birthday party and cannot find a socket.

Charging speeds vary more than capacities. The Oppo K13 5G supports 80W charging, by far the fastest here. The Realme P4x 5G is rated at 45W and the Vivo T4x 5G at 44W, while the Galaxy M17 5G tops out at 25W, so topping up even its smaller battery takes noticeably longer.

Software support is the second priority, and this is where the conventional wisdom needs updating. Samsung has long been the safe recommendation for buyers who keep a phone for years, and models such as the Galaxy A17 5G and the entry-level Galaxy A07 5G do come with long update commitments. But that promise does not extend evenly across Samsung's range: the Galaxy M17 5G, the company's online-focused battery phone, is limited to two Android OS upgrades and four years of security patches. Xiaomi, meanwhile, has quietly improved. The Redmi 15 5G ships with HyperOS 2 based on Android 15 and is promised four years of OS updates and six years of security updates, putting it in the same conversation as Samsung's best. At the other end, the Ai+ Nova 2 Ultra 5G is eligible for only one major OS update and the Lava Blaze Duo 3 5G has limited OS support, which rules both out for anyone planning to hold on to a phone.

Then there is the camera. Indoor photos of kids are one of the hardest jobs you can give a budget phone: light is limited, subjects never sit still, and the camera has to balance shutter speed against noise. Megapixel counts tell you almost nothing here; image processing and stabilisation matter far more.

This is where the Galaxy A17 5G disappoints. Its triple camera pairs a 50MP main sensor with a 5MP ultra-wide and a 2MP macro lens, but the main camera does not have optical image stabilisation, so in a dim room it is forced to choose between slower shutter speeds that blur a wriggling toddler and heavy noise reduction that smears detail. The Galaxy M17 5G does get a 50MP OIS camera, but its shorter update window undercuts the main reason to pick Samsung in the first place. Elsewhere, the Realme P4x 5G's 50MP main and 2MP monochrome setup is the weakest of the big-battery phones, and the Tecno Pop X 5G's image quality drops off noticeably in low light.

That leaves the Redmi 15 5G as our pick. It starts at ₹15,999 and pairs its 7,000mAh battery with a 6.9-inch Full HD+ 144Hz display, a Snapdragon 6s Gen 3 chip, 50MP dual rear cameras, an 8MP selfie camera and an IP64 rating. With its improved update promise it now covers all three of your priorities without stretching the budget, and the money saved is best spent on the 256GB variant, because a family photo library fills 128GB faster than you think.

If charging speed matters more than price, the Oppo K13 5G is the alternative. It starts at ₹19,999 with a Snapdragon 6 Gen 4 chip, a 6.67-inch 120Hz OLED display, 50MP + 2MP rear cameras, a 16MP front camera and that 80W charging, though higher-storage versions can sell above ₹20,000. Buyers on a tighter budget can look at the Vivo T4x 5G from ₹15,499. The one phone we would avoid is the Vivo T5 Lite 5G, whose sluggish everyday performance and pre-installed bloatware outweigh its battery life.

The bottom line: the old rule of 'buy Samsung for updates' no longer settles the question under ₹20,000. For a parent who wants two-day battery life, years of updates and a phone that will hold thousands of family photos, the Redmi 15 5G is the most complete package in the segment right now.
